canonical_title: The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: The complete five-volume gathering of Dick's roughly 120 short stories from 1952 onward, the definitive archive of the short fiction that fed nearly every major PKD novel and film adaptation.
page_summary:
The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 is the standard scholarly edition of Dick's short fiction, assembling essentially all of the roughly 120 stories he wrote, arranged chronologically from his first published work in 1952 through the scattered later pieces. Each volume takes its name from a signature story, and together they run to well over two thousand pages.

This is the seedbed of Dick's entire career. The short stories were where he worked out, quickly and cheaply, the ideas that became the novels: precognition, simulacra, drug-altered perception, android empathy, the small man against the system, and the reality that will not stay fixed. They are also the direct source of the films: 'The Minority Report,' 'We Can Remember It for You Wholesale' (Total Recall), 'Adjustment Team' (The Adjustment Bureau), 'Second Variety' (Screamers), 'Paycheck,' and the stories behind the Electric Dreams series all live here.

For any serious study of Dick, this collection is the foundational document: it lets a reader trace the evolution of his obsessions across three decades and see how repeatedly he returned to a small set of questions about what is real and what is human.
